item.title: Twin Falls In-N-Out shooting suspect identified after 3 killed, 7 wounded
item.description: The suspect, identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

item.title: Trump says Jeanine Pirro "choked" in dropping Reflecting Pool cases
item.description: "She folded like an umbrella," President Trump said of Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.

item.title: Trump comments on calls for Rep. Max Miller to resign amid abuse allegations
item.description: Republican Rep. Max Miller is facing growing calls to resign amid allegations of abuse against his ex-wife and their child. President Trump commented about the situation on Monday. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns reports.

item.title: Cornyn and Tillis say they'll support Blanche for AG after rescinding "anti-weaponization fund"
item.description: Todd Blanche is one step closer to becoming permanent attorney general after he rescinded President Trump's "anti-weaponization fund," earning him the support of Republican Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis. CBS News' Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: Trump says new talks are Iran's "last chance" to make deal
item.description: President Trump on Monday said he was giving Iran a "last chance" to make a deal to end the war through diplomacy. CBS News' Natalie Brand reports.

item.title: New NASA renderings show Earth as lumpy
item.description: From Apollo 11 to Artemis II, space missions have provided numerous images of a beautiful, seemingly smooth and perfectly round Earth. But new NASA renderings show our home looking more like a lumpy potato than a blue marble. Wired magazine senior science editor Brian Kahn joins to discuss.

item.title: Marjorie Taylor Greene, Tucker Carlson float new "America First" movement
item.description: Former Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene posted an image on social media Saturday of a dinner featuring conservative commentator Tucker Carlson, Rep. Thomas Massie and others, stating "the movement has begun." Political strategists Ameshia Cross and Jesse Arm join with analysis.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's diary excerpts read at trial: "I feel like I'm drowning"
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial​ resumed with excerpts from her diary and testimony from doctors who treated Clancy and her children on the night of the murders.

item.title: Coinbase vice chair says he's hopeful Senate will pass crypto regulation bill ahead of recess
item.description: The Senate heads to recess this weekend, meaning time is running out to consider a big crypto regulation bill. The CLARITY Act, which passed the House with bipartisan support in 2025, would give federal agencies new powers to monitor digital assets. Coinbase Vice Chair Ryan VanGrack joins to discuss.

item.title: El-Sayed says he wants to "build a broad coalition" of Democratic voters
item.description: In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed​ and Rep. Haley Stevens are making their final pitches to Democratic voters before Tuesday's Senate primary. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe spoke with El-Sayed and has the latest.

item.title: Sen. Moreno says ex-son-in-law Rep. Max Miller shouldn't serve in Congress amid abuse allegations
item.description: Ohio Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno says his ex-son-in-law, Rep. Max Miller, is dangerous, needs psychiatric care and should no longer serve in Congress. Moreno's daughter has accused Miller of domestic abuse, which he denies. CBS News congressional correspondent Caitlin Huey-Burns reports.

item.title: Trump says Pirro "choked" and "folded like an umbrella" in Reflecting Pool vandalism case
item.description: President Trump on Monday blasted longtime ally and U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro because she moved to drop charges against former Olympian David Hearn, who was accused of vandalizing the Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C. CBS News homeland security correspondent Nicole Sganga has the details.

item.title: The Trump administration's contradictions and contortions on Iran war, Blanche nomination and more
item.description: After President Trump called off a planned military attack against Iran, and GOP holdouts Cornyn and Tillis reached an agreement to support Todd Blanche for attorney general, CBS News chief Washington correspondent Major Garrett says two words come to mind: contradiction and contortion. CBS News' Nancy Cordes and Aaron MacLean report on the latest from the White House.

item.title: 25 states sue Trump administration over latest round of tariffs
item.description: New U.S. tariffs are hurting consumers and businesses, California's attorney general said in filing suit to block levies on 60 countries.

item.title: Senate candidate El-Sayed questions assumption Michigan voters are moderates
item.description: Populist Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens top the Democratic field going into Tuesday's Senate primary. Former Rep. Mike Rogers is running unopposed for the GOP nomination.

item.title: No new Iran negotiations planned despite Trump comments, U.S. officials say
item.description: President Trump, who called Tehran "unbelievably duplicitous," said the talks are the "last chance" for Iran to forge a deal and avoid an escalation.

item.title: Zac Brown Band surprises 37,000 Fenway Park concert fans with free cruises
item.description: Zac Brown Band celebrated their 15th straight sold-out concert at Fenway Park in Boston by giving everyone a free vacation on a cruise ship.

item.title: Trump administration finalizes AI framework, official says
item.description: The order asks AI companies to share previews of powerful new models with the government before they are released to the public.

item.title: Trump says oil companies should cut gas prices after making "too much money"
item.description: President Trump said U.S. oil companies made "too much money" from high oil prices. "I'm not happy about it," he added.

item.title: Could DOJ revive the "anti-weaponization" fund even after Blanche rescinded it?
item.description: GOP Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis formally announced their support for Todd Blanche as attorney general on Monday. This comes after an agreement was reached to end the controversial "anti-weaponization" fund. Rupa Bhattacharyya, legal director at the Institute for Constitutional Advocacy and Protection, joins with analysis.

item.title: Martha Stewart | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: 60 Minutes interviewed media mogul Martha Stewart several times over the years. In 1995, Morley Safer asked about the difference between Martha Stewart the brand and Martha Stewart the person. Stewart replied, "Well, there's not really much of a difference. I am Martha Stewart and my business has become also Martha Stewart. That's the complicated thing for the people who work with me." Today, the American businesswoman turns 85.

item.title: Michigan health officials report 2 deaths among cyclosporiasis cases
item.description: Two Michigan residents who had "significant underlying health conditions" have died after contracting cyclosporiasis, the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services said.

item.title: Cornyn, Tillis back Blanche for attorney general after deal on DOJ fund
item.description: GOP Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina formally announced their support on Monday for Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general.

item.title: What to watch for in SpaceX's first public earnings report this week
item.description: SpaceX will release its first earnings report as a public company on Tuesday in a key test for the company's stuttering stock price.

item.title: ICE sets new Trump-era detention record in July
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detentions reached a record high in July for President Trump's second term, internal data shows. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has the latest.

item.title: Funeral held for family "wiped off the map" in Russian strike
item.description: At least two adults and four children were killed in the strike but the death toll could be higher as all the remains have not yet been formally identified.

item.title: Morocco blames Ceuta border surge on misleading info spread online
item.description: Morocco is blaming a massive surge of migrants​ into Ceuta on various factors, including "malicious exploitation of digital platforms" and the spread of misleading information.

item.title: Ariana Grande pulls out of musical over "endless, ongoing public scrutiny"
item.description: Ariana Grande had been due to star alongside her "Wicked" co-star Jonathan Bailey in a production of "Sunday in the Park with George" in 2027.

item.title: The Footprint
item.description: A woman is murdered in her home and the pivotal clue at the crime scene is a bloody footprint her killer left behind. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty reports.

item.title: "Dead Girls Don't Talk"
item.description: A man charged with murder for poisoning two women tells a friend, "dead girls don't talk." Brave survivors speak out on their behalf. "48 Hours" contributor Jonathan Vigliotti reports.
